messages:
anya: started a small CI experiment to auto-capture traces when KV-cache or batching heuristics change. goal: nsys + perfetto captures, upload to S3, compute a lightweight fingerprint, and surface diffs in the perf dashboard. interested in quick sanity checks and any objections :eyes:

devon: nice. which job did you wire up? is this a nightly or triggered on PRs?

anya: wired into the perf-ci matrix under job 'autocapture-kvbatch'. triggers on PRs that modify runtime/batching or runtime/kvcache, and nightly for full coverage. job link: https://ci.redwood/internal/jobs/autocapture-kvbatch (internal)

samir: curious about capture size. nsys traces blow up for long sequences. do we do a short synthetic workload or real end-to-end?

anya: we run two modes: 1) short synthetic microbench (seq len 64/256, batch sizes 1/8/32) to keep traces small, and 2) on-nightly end-to-end capture capped at 30s. artifacts get compressed and we keep the microbench forever, nightly for 30 days.

maya: can you paste the capture command? makes it easier to validate the flags.

anya: sure — command we settled on for CI microbench:

```
nsys profile --capture-range=nvtx --sample=none
  --output ${CI_ARTIFACT_DIR}/trace_micro.${BUILD_ID}
  --trace=cpu,gpu,cuda,roctx
  --force-overwrite
  --duration=15
  --capture-children true --quiet --stats true --no-stacks
  -- python -m perf_bench.kv_batch_runner --model gpt-small
    --seq-lens 64,256 --batches 1,8,32 --warmup 3 --iters 10
```

ops-bot: uploaded artifact s3://redwood-perf-traces/autocapture/microbench/1865432100/trace_micro.1865432100.qdrep (size: 18.4MB) :white_check_mark:

devon: looks good. how are we generating the fingerprint/diff from the trace? I assume we don't diff raw nsys files.

anya: right. pipeline steps:
- extract kernel timeline & op annotations via perf-parse (in house) -> JSON events
- compute summary vector: per-kernel runtime P50/P95, memory ops, launch overhead, dominant kernels list
- hash the summary to generate a fingerprint
- compare new fingerprint to baseline -> if different, compute a small human-readable diff and flamegraph delta

samir: what about kernel selection regressions? e.g., unexpected kernel variant being chosen after a change in compilation flags. fingerprint should include kernel binary name and launch params.

anya: yep we include kernel name, sm version, grid/block dims, and cu context flags (when available). that helps spot when a new kernel variant appears.

maya: for KV-cache behavior we need to capture KV hit/miss metrics. how are we annotating those?

anya: KV code emits NVTX ranges with tags like 'kv:hit' or 'kv:miss' and counters. perf-parse picks those up and we compute hit-rate per-step. included in the summary vector as a couple floats and a histogram of hits per-step.

devon: CI storage: microbench per-PR forever? might blow up.

anya: plan is microbench artifacts are retained per-PR for 7 days, and promoted to long-term if CI mark says 'baseline snapshot'. nightly artifacts go to 30-day then to cold storage. we also keep only the extracted JSON summary + compressed perfetto slices for UI diff; raw .qdrep only kept for 7 days unless someone requests it.

samir: automation question: how do we decide the baseline for diffs? first green run on the PR or a pinned baseline per-branch?

anya: pinned baseline per-branch. we pin the last known good fingerprint on main (managed by perf-bot). PR diffs are computed against that branch baseline unless the PR updates baseline via explicit LGTM by perf owners.

ci-bot: new perf snapshot created: s3://redwood-perf-traces/autocapture/summaries/1865432100/summary.json (fingerprint: b3f4c9a7)

maya: nice. one more ask: include a quick diff view that highlights kernel-level perf regressions and KV hit-rate delta. if kernel name changed, show previous vs current launch time and caller op.

anya: already on the plan for the dashboard. prototype will show a compact table: kernel_name | prev P95 | new P95 | delta | caller_op | note. also KV hit-rate row and a flamegraph link.

devon: any privacy/security concerns with traces? keys or PII in CUDA debug symbols?

anya: we scrub symbol paths and any environment variables before upload. nothing user-content. artifacts are stored in encrypted S3 bucket with restricted IAM. logs note redaction step.

samir: cool. ready for a short review. I'll run a few PRs through it and report size/false-positives.

anya: thanks — I'll open a PR to add the job definition and the perf-parse extractor. tagging @maya @devon for quick review. :rocket:
